# Sensitivity analysis of the SWiM syntheses (generated — do not edit by hand)

Generated by `code/analysis/sensitivity_analysis.py`. Direction coding (raw coefficient sign and substantive direction) is read from the SWiM documents themselves; nothing was re-coded here.
Conclusion tests were written before the scenarios were run, not before the baseline counts existed (see the script's docstring).

## Headline

**At least one stated conclusion fails under some scenario:** S0 baseline — C_test_no_dominant_sign; S1 drop abstract-only extractions — C_test_no_dominant_sign; S1b drop sparse-audit strong+moderate rows — C_test_no_dominant_sign; S2 drop rows for studies not flagged eligible — C_test_no_dominant_sign; S3 collapse linked reports (same underlying data) — C_test_no_dominant_sign; S4 drop the Family A coding judgment call (S404; S358 left the families under A26) — C_test_no_dominant_sign; S4e recode S879 as Null (household water access alone) — C_test_no_dominant_sign Families A, B and C rest on 13, 3 and 15 studies; the scenarios remove at most 10 of them.

## Why several scenarios change nothing (or not)

- **Abstract-only extractions (10 studies, prefix definition):** none has an `effect_sizes.csv` row, so S1 leaves every family unchanged. It matters for descriptive counts only (below).
- **Linked reports:** 2 definite same-data links; 1 involves a study that has an effect-size row (S366 (Family B)), so S3 changes nothing in A, B or C (only one member of each linked pair has an effect-size row, so there is no second member to remove).
- **Studies with an effect-size row but not flagged eligible (none):** none; S2 removes them.
- **Sparse-audit strong and moderate rows (S1b):** removes 0 study(ies) from the families (none); Family A goes from k = 13 to 13, B from 3 to 3, C from 15 to 15. The sparse-audit signals are heuristics (`05_analysis/descriptive/SPARSE_RECORD_AUDIT_2026-10-04.md`).

Tests: **A** — more than half of the studies are Favourable (concordant with "recognition/eligibility improves access") in the substantive-direction table;
**B** — no study is Unfavourable or Null in substantive direction; **C** — no single category holds a majority, by raw coefficient sign and by substantive direction. The raw sign is the sign of the reported estimate; the substantive direction is its meaning for household access, affordability or equity once the outcome polarity and the exposure pole are taken into account (`05_analysis/effect_sizes/SWIM_DIRECTION_CODING_2026-10-14.csv`). **S4c** recodes S471 (significant in its organisation-only model, not after full adjustment) as Null; **S4e** recodes S879 as Null (household water access alone was null; the 30-point rise was in payment compliance); **S4d** keeps only the studies where the two readings agree ('+' is Favourable, '-' is Unfavourable), which tests whether the Family A and C conclusions depend on the inverted-outcome and restated-pole judgments.

## Descriptive counts with the 10 abstract-only extractions removed

Studies: 1,072 → 1,062. Risk-of-bias tool distribution:

| Tool | All | Without abstract-only | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| MMAT | 195 | 194 | -1 |
| JBI Cross-Sectional | 127 | 125 | -2 |
| CASP Qualitative | 248 | 242 | -6 |
| Legal Framework | 426 | 425 | -1 |
| AMSTAR 2 | 18 | 18 | +0 |
| ROBINS-I | 53 | 53 | +0 |
| RoB 2 | 5 | 5 | +0 |

Every tool population keeps its rank order; the largest reductions are CASP Qualitative (6), JBI Cross-Sectional (2), MMAT (1).

## What this does not test

- The direction coding itself (a judgment by the same AI; a human should re-code a sample).
- Whether other studies belong in the families, or whether unextracted studies would change them.
- Overlap between separate papers that were not flagged as linked (e.g. S526 and S539 both use large US utilities; `linked_reports_2026-09-28.csv` LR09, audit-inferred).
- Any effect size: none is pooled, so there is nothing to test for heterogeneity or publication bias.
